claims.text: Adding 5–10 at.% Al to an Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr–Cr refractory multiprincipal-element alloy promotes selective formation of an alumina scale.
The Al-promoted alumina scale is continuous, adherent, and slow-growing.
An alumina scale impedes oxygen ingress and metal diffusion.
Formation of the alumina scale enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance and material integrity.
Trace Y can enhance the protective effect associated with selective Al oxidation.
The multiprincipal-element matrix regulates oxide nucleation.
The multiprincipal-element matrix suppresses detrimental elemental segregation and thereby preserves oxide-scale continuity.
The alloy without added Al forms heterogeneous Cr-, Ti-, or Zr-rich oxides.
The mixed oxides formed by the Al-free alloy are less continuous than the alumina scale formed by the Al-containing alloy.
The oxide scale on the Al-free alloy is more prone to spallation than the scale on the Al-containing alloy.
The Al-containing alloy will show lower oxidation kinetics, as indicated by reduced weight gain relative to the Al-free baseline.
The Al-containing alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation than the Al-free baseline.
The Al-free baseline will develop a thicker and more inhomogeneous oxide layer than the Al-containing alloy.
The mixed oxide layer on the Al-free baseline will cause more rapid material degradation.
The proposed mechanism should operate in the Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr–Cr-based alloy system from 800°C to 1200°C.
Significant elemental segregation or secondary-phase formation may alter oxidation behavior and scale morphology.
